Fitting adds £650-£910 at a specialist, depending on xDrive complexity. Rebuilt engines include upgraded components addressing the original failure point. 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty is standard on all rebuilt units. Supply & fit available through our UK-wide specialist network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 4 Series 425d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning sign is a rattling or clattering noise from the engine on cold start, which may fade as the engine warms up. Other symptoms include rough idling, reduced performance, and the check engine light illuminating. N47-equipped 425d models (2013-2016) are most affected. Chain stretch typically becomes audible between 60,000-120,000 miles. Ignoring the rattle can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series 425d?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 425d worth £8,000-£18,000, a rebuilt engine at £3,800-£6,500 is a viable investment if you plan to keep the car for two or more years. For sub-£8,000 examples, evaluate a used engine or targeted repair first. Rebuilt engines come with a 12-month warranty and upgraded components. Compare three quotes before committing - pricing varies significantly between suppliers. Supply & fit removes the hassle of finding a specialist yourself.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series 425d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 4 Series 425d engine replacement takes 2-3 days from order to delivery for the engine unit itself. Supply & fit adds 10-14 hours of workshop labour for a 2.0-litre diesel, depending on xDrive complexity. Same-day dispatch available on many used and reconditioned units. Most specialists complete the fit within 2-3 working days. Nationwide delivery means you're not limited to local suppliers.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 425d and 420d engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 425d uses the same 2.0-litre diesel block as the 420d but with a more powerful factory tune - 218-224hp versus 184-190hp. Early 425d models used the N47D20D engine; later models switched to the B47D20B with Euro 6 compliance. 425d power output: 218hp (N47) or 224hp (B47). Both share the same 2.0L displacement and four-cylinder layout. Engine codes are not interchangeable - verify your unit before ordering.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement engine affect my BMW 4 Series 425d's MOT?

acceptedAnswer.text: A correctly fitted replacement engine that meets the original emissions specification will not affect your MOT. All B47D20B engines are Euro 6 compliant; N47D20D engines meet Euro 5 standards. Ensure the replacement engine matches your car's original emissions class. Your specialist will provide emissions documentation with the fit. A like-for-like replacement is fully MOT-legal.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series 425d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 425d joined the 4 Series range as a power-oriented diesel variant, sitting above the 420d and below the six-cylinder 430d/435d. Over its production life, the 425d moved from the N47 to the more robust B47 engine family, bringing improved emissions compliance and reliability.

milestones.description: N47D20D, 2.0L turbo diesel, 218hp, launch of the F32 Coupé 425d
B47D20B, 2.0L turbo diesel, 224hp, introduced as the Euro 6-compliant replacement
B47D20B continues across F32/F33/F36 body styles with 224hp output
425d badge discontinued with the G22 generation; the 420d became the sole four-cylinder diesel offering

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 4 Series 425d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series 425d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 425d's 2.0-litre diesel engines are broadly dependable, but two distinct failure patterns dominate replacement demand. Early N47D20D-equipped cars suffer the notorious timing-chain weakness, while later B47D20B cars see EGR cooler failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 4 Series 425d N47D20D Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The rear-mounted timing chain and plastic tensioner guides are prone to stretch and wear. Poor oil maintenance accelerates the issue. A cold-start rattle is the classic warning sign; ignoring it leads to valve and piston collision, destroying the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner, guides; oil system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Prevents catastrophic failure if caught early; buys another 60k+ miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if chain has already snapped or engine is high-mileage with multiple issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 4 Series 425d (2013-2016) sits in the £8,000-£18,000 bracket. At this value, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine (£4,500-£6,500) represents a viable investment if you plan to keep the car for two or more years. For sub-£8,000 examples, evaluate whether a used engine or targeted chain repair offers better value.
problems.recommendation: If your N47-powered 425d has a timing chain rattle but the engine is otherwise healthy, the specialist chain replacement is the sensible first step - it costs a fraction of a full rebuild and restores reliability. If the chain has already snapped or the car has covered over 140,000 miles, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components is the more cost-effective long-term answer.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N47D20D BMW 4 Series 425d engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Failure - Why the BMW 4 Series 425d B47D20B Needs Attention
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop internal cracks, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust. This can cause white smoke, loss of power, and in extreme cases, a fire risk - a recall was issued for some B47-equipped models.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler, coolant flush, system reset
repairOptions.longevity: Effective fix if caught early; restores emissions compliance
Only necessary if EGR failure has caused secondary damage or engine is high-mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 4 Series 425d (2016-2020) retains £10,000-£22,000 of value. With the car comfortably in the £15,000+ bracket, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is well within the vehicle's value - replacement cost is typically small relative to the car's worth.
problems.recommendation: The B47 is a significantly more robust engine than the N47. If your 425d develops EGR cooler symptoms, have the cooler replaced promptly - it's a straightforward fix that costs under £1,200 at a specialist. A full engine replacement is rarely required unless the cooler failure has been ignored and caused collateral damage.
